verdict.rationale: An official, first-party MCP server is documented (gladia-probe-4), which lets users drive Gladia from an AI assistant in natural language. The evidence is only a bare probe noting the docs page exists, so the server's tools and depth are unproven. The LLM-on-audio feature (gladia-docs-2) applies prompts to transcript content rather than controlling the product, so it adds little here. Missing for 10: a native natural-language command interface in the product itself, documentation of the MCP server's tools and supported operations, and hands-on or independent confirmation that NL-driven operation works end to end.
